subject: Request: multi-arch variant fallback & version pin exception
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Alice Yang <alice@acme.ai>
Date: 2027-09-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Request: multi-arch variant fallback & version pin exception

Hi team,

Acme AI wants to test Aurora-v2 (multi-arch build: x86 + arm) as the default serving model for their POC. They reported a small increase in hallucination rate on long-context prompts (seen only on arm builds) and asked us to keep Aurora-v1 available as an immediate fallback for their traffic while they validate.

Ask: can we grant a temporary version-pin exception for Acme's account so traffic can fallback to Aurora-v1 when arm-variant inference latency or quality breaches thresholds? I also want a small canary rollout (5% traffic) of Aurora-v2 on arm nodes first.

Constraints to consider:
- Security/compliance: Acme will be running in our Dedicated environment (no external data sharing).
- Capacity: infra has limited arm nodes next quarter.
- Observability: need token-level quality delta + latency SLO per region.

Please reply with feasibility and what controls we need (SLO gates, rollout window, duration of exception). Acme is asking for a formal exception doc for their procurement team by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Head of Sales, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Alice Yang <alice@acme.ai>, Infra Ops <infra-ops@cloudvendor.com>
Date: 2027-09-12T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: multi-arch variant fallback & version pin exception

Marissa —

We can support a per-account routing policy that pins to a primary model and falls back to a secondary variant on quality or latency triggers. Implementation notes:

- Technical approach: add a per-customer route with prioritized model list [aurora-v2-arm, aurora-v2-x86, aurora-v1-x86]. Fallback executed when: 95th latency > X ms OR quality score (eval metric) drops > Y points over rolling window.
- Canary: we can gate 5% to arm nodes using existing traffic-split feature.
- Telemetry: need an eval set from Acme (we currently lack good long-context prompts). Without that, quality gating will be noisy.
- Capacity: arm nodes scarce; we can schedule the canary during low-traffic hours and allocate burst credits. Infra Ops (cc) will need to confirm availability.

I can draft the exception policy and the rollout config. Rishi — can you produce a quick compatibility run and a short quality delta report for the arm build? If we get that, I'll wire the traffic policy and create the rollout plan.

- Dev
Senior SW Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Alice Yang <alice@acme.ai>
Date: 2027-09-13T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: multi-arch variant fallback & version pin exception

Attached is a short compatibility + quality snapshot for Aurora-v2 arm vs x86 using Acme's anonymized long-context sample (50 prompts). Summary:

- Latency (p95): arm build ~ 210ms vs x86 ~ 160ms on the same sequence length distribution.
- Quality: measured using Acme's relevance metric (A->B): arm build shows a -2.3 point delta vs x86 on long-context (>2k tokens). Aurora-v1 (x86) outperforms both on hallucination rate in this test set.
- Observations: the arm quantization path increases variance on certain attention kernels; we saw a small KV-cache misalignment that can be mitigated by a patch (PR link in related_links).

I attached compat_report_aurora_v2.pdf and kv_cache_sample.json with examples. My recommendation: allow the exception with the following safeguards:
1) Canary 5% on arm nodes for 72 hours.
2) Quality gate: if rolling eval delta > 1.5 points worse for 6 hours, auto-fallback to aurora-v1 for that account.
3) Latency gate: if 95th percentile > 250ms for 4 hours, fallback.
4) Post-canary: run targeted A/B eval for 48h then reassess pin.

If infra can schedule the arm capacity, this is feasible.

—Rishi
Applied ML Engineer — Inference
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Yang <alice@acme.ai>
Date: 2027-09-13T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: multi-arch variant fallback & version pin exception

Thanks Rishi and Dev — this looks reasonable. A couple of product asks before we surface to Acme and procurement:

- Please add explicit success criteria for the 72h canary (concrete numbers for the eval metric and latency). For procurement we should state: "if criteria met, exception duration 30 days; otherwise auto-revert."
- Add a rollback playbook (who executes fallback, who notifies the customer, and a runbook snippet for infra).
- Include the monitoring dashboard link and the alert routing (pager/team) in the exception doc.

Dev — can you draft the exception document with these bullets and include the JIRA ticket so we can track? I can own the customer communication once the draft is ready.

Laura
Product Manager, Model Platform
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Yang <alice@acme.ai>
Date: 2027-09-14T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: multi-arch variant fallback & version pin exception

Team — thanks for the fast turnaround. Action items + decisions:

1) Approve temporary per-account pin exception for Acme AI effective immediately for canary (5% traffic on arm) with the safeguards Rishi recommended.
2) Dev to produce the exception doc (include success criteria: eval delta <= 1.5 points over 72h; p95 latency < 240ms) and the rollback playbook. Link the JIRA INF-3245.
3) Infra Ops to confirm scheduled arm capacity by EOD tomorrow (cc Infra Ops).
4) Lauren will send procurement-facing exception summary to Acme once doc is ready.

Marissa
Marissa Cole | Head of Sales, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
